title: The Two Mothers and the Living Child (TE)
summary: Two women claim the same infant. Birbal orders the baby cut in half, exposing the real mother through her unconditional sacrifice.
full_text:
Two women, Leela and Radha, who lived in the same village house, appeared before Emperor Akbar's imperial court, weeping hysterically and wrestling over a healthy, crying six-month-old baby boy.

Leela wailed: 'Sire! This is my child, born of my body! Radha's baby died three days ago, and in the dead of night, she crept into my room, took my living baby from my cradle, and replaced it with her dead child!'

Radha screamed back: 'Lies, Your Majesty! She is the one whose child died! This living baby is my flesh and blood!'

There were no witnesses, and the village elders could not determine which woman was telling the truth.

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'How can this be settled without witnesses?'

Birbal looked at the two weeping women, summoned a palace executioner with a heavy, gleaming scimitar, and announced in a cold, solemn voice:

'Since both women claim the child, and the court cannot favor one without evidence, justice demands equal division. Executioner, step forward! Draw your sword, cut this baby into two equal halves, and give one half to each mother!'

Radha folded her arms and said coldly: 'A fair judgment, Sire! If I cannot have the whole child, neither shall she! Cut the boy in two!'

Hearing this, Leela let out a piercing shriek of agony. She threw herself upon the floor at the feet of the executioner, crying:

'No! No! Do not strike my baby with a sword! Give the child to Radha! Let her keep him, let her raise him, but let my baby live!'

Birbal immediately raised his hand: 'Executioner, sheath your blade!'

Birbal lifted the weeping child and placed him into Leela's arms:

'Here is the true mother. An imposter cares only for spite and possession, and would rather see the child slaughtered than lose her claim. But the true mother loves her child so deeply that she would rather endure the agony of separation than see a single hair on his head harmed.'

Akbar ordered Radha imprisoned for her wicked fraud, awarded the child to Leela with an imperial grant, and praised Birbal's profound insight into the maternal heart.
